name: ByteLeap

product.what_it_is: A decentralised GPU cloud (RTX 3090 through H100/H200/B200, bare metal or VM) that sources hardware from third-party operators via SN128; miners earn lease scores mainly when their machines are actually rented by paying customers, and idle workers score zero.
product.quality_rationale: RAISED from 45. Published per-GPU-hour rates and a reported ~95% utilisation across more than 1,200 deployed GPUs indicate a storefront that real customers were actually using, and the incentive design pays on genuine leases rather than idle capacity. Held at 50 and no higher because the public site byteleap.ai is still a one-line shell with no catalogue, the host-api specs endpoint still rejects GET, the miner repository is dormant (77 days since last commit), and the supporting figures are 10 months old.

revenue.basis: ByteLeap states it has rental revenue and published per-GPU-hour rates, but the only volume figures available are from December 2025 (1,216 GPUs deployed, 1,157 rented) and the GPU mix is only partly disclosed (609 RTX 5090 of 1,216; the remaining ~600 units span 3090/H100/H200/B200 at rates from $0.26 to $4.80 per GPU-hour). Annualising would require guessing the mix for roughly half the fleet and assuming a 10-month-old utilisation figure still holds, so any ARR I produced would be invented. arr_usd deliberately left null. growth.evidence: No comparable dated revenue figures. The only volume datapoint is December 2025 (1,216 GPUs, ~95% utilisation); the only intervening event is an August 2026 submission of commercial-revenue documentation to restore emissions. Against that, the miner repository has gone dormant (77 days since last commit as of 2026-10-27, versus 'last push 11 Aug 2026' in the prior record), which is a negative operational signal.

customers.evidence: No customer names. Customer existence is inferred from the reported ~95% utilisation across 1,157 rented GPUs in December 2025 and from the incentive design, under which idle workers score zero on the lease component. No count, segment breakdown or named account has ever been published.

buybacks.mechanism: ByteLeap states that revenue from its GPU rental business is used to buy back SN128 alpha. No percentage of revenue, no schedule, no wallet address and no executed-purchase ledger has been published.
buybacks.evidence: subnetalpha.ai/subnet/byteleap (fetched 2026-10-27, verbatim): 'ByteLeap says part of that revenue has gone into alpha buybacks' and 'ByteLeap has said that the revenue from its rental business goes towards buying back SN128 alpha'. Both are team self-reports relayed by a secondary index; I found no first-party buyback dashboard, address or transaction list, and byteleap.ai carries no buyback text. Recorded as 'announced' rather than 'active' for that reason.

notes: CHANGE vs 2026-10-08, and it is a correction rather than a new event. I still did not record an ARR: the volume data is from December 2025, the fleet mix is only half-disclosed, and ByteLeap's own marketing elsewhere claims '5000+ active GPU servers' which contradicts the 1,216 figure, so any annualisation would be guesswork.
